These selected outputs show how field ecology, environmental stress biology and molecular approaches have developed into questions about biological organisation and resilience.

## Selected peer-reviewed publications

::: {.publication-showcase}
<p class="publication-theme">Non-model ecotoxicogenomics resource</p>

### De novo transcriptome assembly and annotation of the common freshwater amphipod (*Gammarus pulex*): a valuable resource for ecotoxicogenomics

<p class="publication-meta"><strong>Escobar-Sierra, C.</strong>, Hassan, S., Weichert, F. G., Aronsson, H., Lampert, K. P., Hollert, H., Backhaus, T., & Inostroza, P. A. (2025). <em>Scientific Data</em>, 12, 1502.</p>

::: {.publication-visual}
![](assets/images/publications/gammarus-transcriptome-workflow.webp){fig-alt="Workflow summarising raw-read processing, de novo transcriptome assembly, validation and annotation for the Gammarus pulex transcriptome resource."}
:::

<p class="publication-caption">Study visual: Fig. 2 from Escobar-Sierra et al. (2025), CC BY 4.0.</p>

<p class="publication-why"><strong>Why it matters.</strong> An open molecular resource designed to enable reproducible ecotoxicogenomics in a widely used non-model freshwater sentinel.</p>

<p class="publication-links">[DOI →](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-05872-2)</p>
:::

::: {.publication-showcase}
<p class="publication-theme">Comparative multi-tissue fish transcriptomics</p>

### Unraveling the molecular mechanisms of fish physiological response to freshwater salinization: A comparative multi-tissue transcriptomic study in a river polluted by potash mining

<p class="publication-meta"><strong>Escobar-Sierra, C.</strong>, Cañedo-Argüelles, M., Vinyoles, D., & Lampert, K. P. (2024). <em>Environmental Pollution</em>, 357, 124400.</p>

::: {.publication-visual}
![](assets/images/publications/freshwater-salinisation-graphical-abstract.webp){fig-alt="Graphical abstract summarising comparative multi-tissue transcriptomic responses of fish to freshwater salinisation."}
:::

<p class="publication-caption">Study visual: graphical abstract from Escobar-Sierra et al. (2024), CC BY-NC.</p>

<p class="publication-why"><strong>Why it matters.</strong> Connected environmentally realistic exposure with tissue-specific and shared molecular response mechanisms across brain, gill and liver.</p>

<p class="publication-links">[DOI →](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2024.124400)</p>
:::

::: {.publication-showcase}
<p class="publication-theme">Field-based de novo transcriptomics</p>

### Field application of de novo transcriptomic analysis to evaluate the effects of sublethal freshwater salinization on *Gasterosteus aculeatus* in urban streams

<p class="publication-meta"><strong>Escobar-Sierra, C.</strong> & Lampert, K. P. (2024). <em>PLOS ONE</em>, 19, e0298213.</p>

::: {.publication-visual}
![](assets/images/publications/field-denovo-transcriptomics-graphical-abstract.webp){fig-alt="Graphical abstract summarising field application of de novo transcriptomics to evaluate sublethal freshwater salinisation in wild fish."}
:::

<p class="publication-caption">Study visual: graphical abstract from the [doctoral thesis](https://kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/75069/), Chapter 1, CC BY-NC.</p>

<p class="publication-why"><strong>Why it matters.</strong> Demonstrated how de novo transcriptomics can recover mechanistic sublethal responses directly from wild fish under complex field conditions.</p>

<p class="publication-links">[DOI →](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0298213)</p>
:::

::: {.publication-showcase}
<p class="publication-theme">Multiple-stressor theory</p>

### The Asymmetric Response Concept explains ecological consequences of multiple stressor exposure and release

<p class="publication-meta">Vos, M., Hering, D., Gessner, M. O., et al., <strong>Escobar-Sierra, C.</strong>, et al. (2023). <em>Science of the Total Environment</em>, 872, 162196.</p>

<p class="publication-why"><strong>Why it matters.</strong> Contributed to a broader conceptual framework for understanding why ecological response to stressor increase and release need not follow the same trajectory.</p>

<p class="publication-links">[DOI →](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2023.162196)</p>
:::

::: {.publication-showcase}
<p class="publication-theme">Ecology meets omics</p>

### Metabolomics unravels grazing interactions under nutrient enrichment from aquaculture

<p class="publication-meta"><strong>Escobar-Sierra, C.</strong>, de Kock, W., Hasler-Sheetal, H., Holmer, M., Chatzigeorgiou, G., Tsapakis, M., & Apostolaki, E. T. (2023). <em>Diversity</em>, 15, 31.</p>

::: {.publication-visual}
![](assets/images/publications/aquaculture-metabolomics-figure5.png){fig-alt="Published Figure 5 showing the Pattern Hunter analysis for Paracentrotus lividus and the top 25 metabolite spectra bins associated with distance from aquaculture nutrient enrichment."}
:::

<p class="publication-caption">Study visual: Fig. 5 from Escobar-Sierra et al. (2023), CC BY 4.0.</p>

<p class="publication-why"><strong>Why it matters.</strong> An early integration of ecological experimentation with an omics approach, linking aquaculture-associated nutrient enrichment to community-level metabolic responses.</p>

<p class="publication-links">[DOI →](https://doi.org/10.3390/d15010031)</p>
:::
